title: The workspace fails to function properly and causes the Antimalware Service Executable process to have a high CPU footprint on startup

judgment.rationale: The author reports that starting a workspace causes Antimalware Service Executable to use about half the CPU and the Workspace configuration window does not open. A maintainer requested /bugreport, but the reporter said the UI falsely claimed a ZIP was generated and none appeared. Do not repeat the failed archive request; ask for a short, non-sensitive reproduction and duration instead.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys 0.84.1, auto-update, running as administrator, and Workspaces.
The body says starting a workspace triggers high Antimalware Service Executable CPU and the configuration window remains absent.
Another commenter says they have the same issue.
The maintainer requested /bugreport, but the author reported that the button displayed success without creating a ZIP.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact workspace launch path and CPU-duration behavior in text; do not ask the reporter to repeat the bug-report action that failed.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report does not establish whether Workspaces, Windows Defender scanning, or a workspace content issue causes the CPU spike. No fix hypothesis is justified before a minimal reproduction is available.

issue_context.summary: Starting a Workspaces workspace reportedly leaves the configuration window closed and causes Antimalware Service Executable to use about half the CPU.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.84.1, auto-update, and running as administrator.
One other commenter reports the same issue.
A maintainer requested a PowerToys bug report archive; the author replied that the report button said it created a ZIP but no file appeared on the desktop.
No workspace contents, CPU duration, exact launch action, or current-version test are stated.
inferences: The CPU load could be Defender scanning workspace-launched content or could coincide with a Workspaces startup failure; the report does not distinguish them.
Because the requested bug-report ZIP could not be generated, a narrowly scoped textual sequence is preferable to repeating that request.
issue_context.analysis: Request only the missing observable facts needed to reproduce: launch method, duration, and whether CPU settles after cancelling or restarting. Avoid asking for personal diagnostic data or another unsuccessful archive.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live body and both comments, including the failed /bugreport response.
No linked fix work or more specific code path is identified by the issue.

information_gaps.information: How the workspace is started, what applications/files it contains, whether the configuration window ever appears, and how long high CPU use continues.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a Workspace Editor launch failure from Defender scanning files or applications launched by the workspace.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please describe the start action and workspace contents by application type only, note whether the window appears, and state whether CPU use settles after waiting or after stopping the launch. Do not include usernames, file paths, or diagnostic archives.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same behavior occurs on a current supported PowerToys version.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report uses 0.84.1 and is old enough that Workspace startup behavior may have changed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please include the version shown in PowerToys Settings > About after checking the same workspace launch.

comment.body:
The report says starting a workspace leaves its configuration window closed while Antimalware Service Executable uses about half the CPU. We saw your note that the Report Bug button said a ZIP was created but no file appeared, so please do not repeat that step. Could you instead share:
- The exact action used to start the workspace and whether it contains applications or files (application types are enough).
- Whether the window ever appears and how long the CPU use continues, or whether it settles after stopping the launch.
- The current PowerToys version.
Avoid sharing usernames, file paths, or other personal diagnostic data.
